specialties.why: Sources describe COL3A1 variant confirmation as central to diagnosis, and genetic testing as essential to confirming vEDS.
specialties.plain: A genetics team can confirm and explain the COL3A1 gene result.

specialties.subspecialty: Connective tissue disease aortic and arterial program
specialties.why: A source describes a multidisciplinary connective tissue disease aortic program at a high-volume center.
specialties.plain: Look for blood vessel surgeons who work in a program for connective tissue conditions.

specialties.why: A case report describes interventional radiology and vascular surgery working jointly on a vEDS patient.
specialties.plain: Some centers have imaging-guided procedure doctors who team up with vascular surgeons.

specialties.why: A review says vEDS management is complex, needs multiple specialists, and recommends identifying and creating a care team.
specialties.plain: vEDS care needs several kinds of doctors working together.

centerCapabilities.text: A multidisciplinary connective tissue disease aortic program within a high-volume aortic center.
centerCapabilities.plain: A program where many specialists treat connective tissue conditions together.

centerCapabilities.text: Ability to provide an individual emergency care plan (a "vascular EDS passport") stating the diagnosis.
centerCapabilities.plain: The center can give you an emergency card or plan that names your condition.

centerCapabilities.text: Experience with many confirmed vEDS patients, such as a national diagnostic service reporting on 180 molecularly confirmed patients.
centerCapabilities.plain: The center has seen many people with confirmed vEDS.

centerCapabilities.text: Joint vascular surgery and interventional radiology teams working together on arterial problems in vEDS.
centerCapabilities.plain: Surgeons and radiology doctors at the same center work together.

centerCapabilities.text: Participation in vEDS or rare vascular disease registries, such as RaDiCo-SED-VASC or the VASCERN registries.
centerCapabilities.plain: The center takes part in research registries for rare blood vessel diseases.

redFlags.text: A resource that offers care by a single clinician with no access to a wider specialist team is a poor fit, since sources describe vEDS care as multispecialty.
redFlags.plain: Be cautious if only one doctor is involved and there is no team.

redFlags.text: A center that does not provide or support an individual emergency care plan or vEDS passport.
redFlags.plain: Be cautious if the center cannot give you an emergency care plan.

redFlags.text: A genetics service that considers only sequencing, without copy-number analysis when sequencing is negative but suspicion persists, may miss some COL3A1 variants.
redFlags.plain: Be cautious if a genetic lab will not look for large missing gene pieces.

redFlags.text: A registry or study with limited geographic coverage, such as one listed as national, may not accept people from other countries.
redFlags.plain: Check whether a study or registry takes people from where you live.

trialEligibility.text: Listings often ask for a molecularly confirmed vEDS diagnosis with a pathogenic COL3A1 variant.
trialEligibility.plain: Studies often want a gene test that confirms vEDS.

trialEligibility.text: Listings may specify the type of COL3A1 variant; reported variants include sequence changes and whole-exon deletions.
trialEligibility.plain: Studies may ask which exact gene change you have.

trialEligibility.text: Registry and cohort listings state recruiting status and geographic coverage, for example RaDiCo-SED-VASC, listed as national and recruiting.
trialEligibility.plain: Studies list whether they are enrolling and which area they cover.

supportNeeds.text: Patient-led vEDS organizations may offer a helpline and community input into research, such as Annabelle's Challenge.
supportNeeds.plain: A patient group can offer a helpline and a voice in research.

supportNeeds.text: Help preparing an emergency care plan or vEDS passport that states the diagnosis.
supportNeeds.plain: You may need help making an emergency card that names your condition.

supportNeeds.text: Specialist vEDS services described in sources are national centers (such as Sheffield and Paris), so travel and lodging help may be needed.
supportNeeds.plain: Specialist centers may be far away, so you may need travel help.

supportNeeds.text: vEDS is autosomal dominant and family history matters, so relatives may seek genetic counseling and testing.
supportNeeds.plain: Family members may want genetic counseling, which can cost money.

questions.text: Do you have experience caring for people with vEDS and COL3A1 variants?
Can you work with my other specialists as part of a coordinated care team?
Do you provide an individual emergency care plan or vEDS passport?
Do you have a multidisciplinary connective tissue program that includes vascular surgery?
Does this study require a confirmed COL3A1 variant, and does it accept my specific variant?
Is this study or registry currently recruiting, and does it accept participants from my country?
Do you offer a helpline or help finding vEDS specialists?
Do you connect patients with research studies or registries for vEDS?
